Force System Resultants

Statics
ENGI 10120 problems
We’ll work through these together in class.
Problem 1
Ch. 4 · Q1 — Moment of a force, scalar formulation
A horizontal cantilever beam is built into a wall at $O$ and extends $2.5\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right to its free end $A$. A vertical force $F = 360\ \mathrm{N}$ acts downward at $A$. Take counterclockwise moments as positive.
Cantilever beam with a vertical end load
Determine the moment of $F$ about point $O$ (counterclockwise positive).
Solution
-900 N·m
Free-body diagram
Beam isolated at O with the force and its moment arm
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the beam by itself with point $O$ at the left end, the $360\ \mathrm{N}$ force pointing down at $A$, and a dashed line along the force's line of action.
Step 2List knowns: $F = 360\ \mathrm{N}$ downward at $A$, and the distance $OA = 2.5\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 3List the unknown: The moment $M_O$ of $F$ about point $O$, with its sense of rotation.
Step 4Isolate the body: The only applied load considered is $F$ at $A$; the wall reactions at $O$ pass through $O$ or are not part of the question, so they do not enter the moment of $F$.
Step 5Set the sign convention: Use $x$ to the right, $y$ up, and counterclockwise moments positive.
Step 6Find the moment arm: $F$ is vertical and the beam is horizontal, so the perpendicular distance from $O$ to the line of action of $F$ is $d = 2.5\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 7Write the governing equation: For a 2-D force the magnitude of the moment is $M_O = F\,d$, because $d$ is measured perpendicular to the line of action.
Step 8Decide the sense: Imagine the beam pinned at $O$; a downward push at the right end rotates it clockwise, so the moment carries a negative sign.
Step 9Substitute numbers: $$M_O = -(360\ \mathrm{N})(2.5\ \mathrm{m})$$
Step 10Compute: $$M_O = -900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11State the result: $M_O = 900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Step 12Check units and size: $\mathrm{N}\times\mathrm{m} = \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, and a few hundred newtons acting a couple of metres away should give a moment of several hundred $\mathrm{N\cdot m}$, which it does.
Worked Solution
Beam isolated at O with the force and its moment arm
**Given:** $F = 360\ \mathrm{N}$ (down) at $A$; $d = 2.5\ \mathrm{m}$. **Find:** $M_O$. The line of action of $F$ is vertical and the beam is horizontal, so the perpendicular distance from $O$ to the line of action is $d = 2.5\ \mathrm{m}$. Imagining the beam pinned at $O$, the downward force at the right end turns it clockwise, so the moment is negative: $$M_O = -F\,d = -(360\ \mathrm{N})(2.5\ \mathrm{m}) = -900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $M_O = 900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Problem 2
Ch. 4 · Q2 — Moment of an inclined force by components
An L-shaped frame is fixed to the ground at $O$. A vertical column rises $3\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$ to corner $B$, and a horizontal arm runs $4\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right from $B$ to $A$. A force $F = 650\ \mathrm{N}$ acts at $A$, directed down and to the right along a line with slope 5 vertical to 12 horizontal (a 5-12-13 triangle). Take counterclockwise moments as positive.
L-shaped frame with an inclined force at A
Determine the moment of $F$ about point $O$ (counterclockwise positive).
Solution
-2800 N·m
Free-body diagram
Frame isolated at O with the force resolved into components at A
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the frame alone with $O$ marked, and replace the inclined force at $A$ by a horizontal component $F_x$ and a vertical component $F_y$.
Step 2List knowns: $F = 650\ \mathrm{N}$ on a 5-12-13 slope (down and right), $OB = 3\ \mathrm{m}$, $BA = 4\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 3List the unknown: The moment $M_O$ of $F$ about $O$ and its sense.
Step 4Set axes and sign convention: Origin at $O$, $x$ right, $y$ up, counterclockwise positive, so $A$ is at $(4,\,3)\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 5Resolve the horizontal component: The horizontal leg of the slope triangle is 12, so $$F_x = 650\left(\tfrac{12}{13}\right) = 600\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(to the right)}$$
Step 6Resolve the vertical component: The vertical leg is 5, so $$F_y = -650\left(\tfrac{5}{13}\right) = -250\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(downward)}$$
Step 7Find the moment arms: $F_y$ acts along the vertical line $x = 4\ \mathrm{m}$, so its arm is $4\ \mathrm{m}$; $F_x$ acts along the horizontal line $y = 3\ \mathrm{m}$, so its arm is $3\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 8Write the governing equation: By the principle of moments the moment of $F$ equals the sum of the moments of its components, $$M_O = x\,F_y - y\,F_x$$
Step 9Substitute numbers: $$M_O = (4\ \mathrm{m})(-250\ \mathrm{N}) - (3\ \mathrm{m})(600\ \mathrm{N})$$
Step 10Evaluate each term: $$M_O = -1000\ \mathrm{N\cdot m} - 1800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11Compute: $$M_O = -2800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12State the result: $M_O = 2.80(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Step 13Check reasonableness: Pinned at $O$, a pull to the right at the top and a push down on the right side both rotate the frame clockwise, so the two terms should have the same (negative) sign, and they do.
Worked Solution
Frame isolated at O with the force resolved into components at A
**Given:** $A(4,\,3)\ \mathrm{m}$ measured from $O$; $F = 650\ \mathrm{N}$ on a 5-12-13 slope, down and to the right. **Components:** $F_x = +650\left(\tfrac{12}{13}\right) = 600\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_y = -650\left(\tfrac{5}{13}\right) = -250\ \mathrm{N}$. **Principle of moments** (CCW $+$), $M_O = x\,F_y - y\,F_x$: $$M_O = (4\ \mathrm{m})(-250\ \mathrm{N}) - (3\ \mathrm{m})(600\ \mathrm{N}) = -1000 - 1800 = -2800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ Both components turn the frame clockwise about $O$. $M_O = 2.80(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Problem 3
Ch. 4 · Q3 — Resultant moment of a coplanar force system
A bent bar is pinned at $O$. It runs horizontally to the right from $O$ through $A$ to $B$, with $OA = 2\ \mathrm{m}$ and $AB = 3\ \mathrm{m}$, then turns vertically upward from $B$ to $C$ with $BC = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$. Three forces act on it: $F_1 = 500\ \mathrm{N}$ straight down at $A$; $F_2 = 800\ \mathrm{N}$ at $B$, directed down and to the right at $45^{\circ}$ below the horizontal; and $F_3 = 600\ \mathrm{N}$ at $C$, directed up and to the left at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Take counterclockwise moments as positive.
Bent bar OABC with three applied forces
Determine the resultant moment of the three forces about point $O$ (counterclockwise positive).
Solution
-1550 N·m
Free-body diagram
Bar isolated at O with every force resolved into x and y components
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the bar alone with $O$ marked, $F_1$ at $A$, and $F_2$ and $F_3$ each replaced by horizontal and vertical components at $B$ and $C$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $F_1 = 500\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_2 = 800\ \mathrm{N}$ at $45^{\circ}$, $F_3 = 600\ \mathrm{N}$ at $30^{\circ}$; $OA = 2\ \mathrm{m}$, $AB = 3\ \mathrm{m}$, $BC = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$. Find $(M_R)_O$.
Step 3Isolate the body: The applied forces are $F_1$, $F_2$ and $F_3$; the pin reaction acts through $O$ and so has no moment about $O$.
Step 4Set axes and sign convention: Origin at $O$, $x$ right, $y$ up, counterclockwise positive. Then $A(2,0)$, $B(5,0)$ and $C(5,1.5)\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 5Resolve $F_2$ in $x$: $$F_{2x} = 800\cos45^{\circ} = 565.7\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(right)}$$
Step 6Resolve $F_2$ in $y$: $$F_{2y} = -800\sin45^{\circ} = -565.7\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(down)}$$
Step 7Resolve $F_3$ in $x$: $$F_{3x} = -600\cos30^{\circ} = -519.6\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(left)}$$
Step 8Resolve $F_3$ in $y$: $$F_{3y} = 600\sin30^{\circ} = 300\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(up)}$$
Step 9Write the governing equation: The resultant moment is the sum of the moments of all components, $$(M_R)_O = \sum\left(x\,F_y - y\,F_x\right)$$
Step 10Moment of $F_1$: Its arm is $2\ \mathrm{m}$ and it turns the bar clockwise, $$M_1 = (2)(-500) = -1000\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11Moment of $F_2$: $F_{2x}$ acts along the line $OB$ through $O$ (zero arm); $F_{2y}$ has a $5\ \mathrm{m}$ arm, $$M_2 = (5)(-565.7) = -2828.4\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12Moment of $F_3$: $F_{3y}$ has a $5\ \mathrm{m}$ arm and $F_{3x}$ a $1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ arm, both counterclockwise, $$M_3 = (5)(300) - (1.5)(-519.6) = 2279.4\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 13Sum the moments: $$(M_R)_O = -1000 - 2828.4 + 2279.4 = -1549\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 14State the result: $(M_R)_O = 1.55(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Step 15Check reasonableness: The two downward forces act clockwise and total about $3830\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; $F_3$ opposes them with about $2280\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, so a net clockwise moment of about $1550\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ is sensible.
Worked Solution
Bar isolated at O with every force resolved into x and y components
**Coordinates from $O$:** $A(2,0)$, $B(5,0)$, $C(5,1.5)\ \mathrm{m}$. **Components:** $F_{1y} = -500\ \mathrm{N}$; $F_{2x} = 800\cos45^{\circ} = 565.7\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_{2y} = -800\sin45^{\circ} = -565.7\ \mathrm{N}$; $F_{3x} = -600\cos30^{\circ} = -519.6\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_{3y} = 600\sin30^{\circ} = 300\ \mathrm{N}$. **Moments** (CCW $+$), using $M = xF_y - yF_x$ for each force: $M_1 = (2)(-500) = -1000\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; $M_2 = (5)(-565.7) - (0)(565.7) = -2828.4\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ ($F_{2x}$ passes through $O$); $M_3 = (5)(300) - (1.5)(-519.6) = 1500 + 779.4 = 2279.4\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$. $$(M_R)_O = -1000 - 2828.4 + 2279.4 = -1549\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $(M_R)_O = 1.55(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Problem 4
Ch. 4 · Q4 — Cross product r × F
A rigid arm lies in the $x$–$y$ plane with one end at the origin $O$ and the other end at $A(0.4,\ 0.3,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$. A force $\mathbf{F} = \{-80\,\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ acts at $A$.
Arm in the x–y plane with a vertical force at A
Using the cross product $\mathbf{M}_O = \mathbf{r}_{OA}\times\mathbf{F}$, determine the magnitude of the moment of $\mathbf{F}$ about $O$.
Solution
40.0 N·m
Free-body diagram
Position vector, force vector and moment vector at O
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the $x$, $y$, $z$ axes, the position vector $\mathbf{r}_{OA}$ from $O$ to $A$ in the $x$–$y$ plane, and the force $\mathbf{F}$ pointing in the $-z$ direction at $A$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $A(0.4,\,0.3,\,0)\ \mathrm{m}$ and $\mathbf{F} = \{-80\,\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$. Find the magnitude $M_O$.
Step 3Write the position vector: $\mathbf{r}$ runs from $O$ to a point on the line of action of $\mathbf{F}$, so $$\mathbf{r}_{OA} = \{0.4\,\mathbf{i} + 0.3\,\mathbf{j} + 0\,\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 4Write the governing equation: The vector formulation of the moment is $\mathbf{M}_O = \mathbf{r}_{OA}\times\mathbf{F}$ (order matters).
Step 5Set up the determinant: $$\mathbf{M}_O = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0.4 & 0.3 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & -80\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 6Expand the $\mathbf{i}$ component: $$M_x = r_yF_z - r_zF_y = (0.3)(-80) - (0)(0) = -24\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 7Expand the $\mathbf{j}$ component: Remember the minus sign on the middle term, $$M_y = -\left(r_xF_z - r_zF_x\right) = -\left[(0.4)(-80) - 0\right] = +32\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 8Expand the $\mathbf{k}$ component: $$M_z = r_xF_y - r_yF_x = (0.4)(0) - (0.3)(0) = 0$$
Step 9Assemble the vector: $$\mathbf{M}_O = \{-24\,\mathbf{i} + 32\,\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 10Compute the magnitude: $$M_O = \sqrt{(-24)^2 + (32)^2} = 40.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11Check with the scalar method: $\mathbf{F}$ is perpendicular to the arm, whose length is $\sqrt{0.4^2 + 0.3^2} = 0.5\ \mathrm{m}$, so $M_O = (80)(0.5) = 40\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, which agrees.
Worked Solution
Position vector, force vector and moment vector at O
**Given:** $\mathbf{r}_{OA} = \{0.4\,\mathbf{i} + 0.3\,\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $\mathbf{F} = \{-80\,\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$. $$\mathbf{M}_O = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0.4 & 0.3 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & -80\end{vmatrix} = \left[(0.3)(-80) - 0\right]\mathbf{i} - \left[(0.4)(-80) - 0\right]\mathbf{j} + \left[0 - 0\right]\mathbf{k} = \{-24\,\mathbf{i} + 32\,\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $$M_O = \sqrt{(-24)^2 + (32)^2} = 40.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ Check: $\mathbf{F}\perp\mathbf{r}$, so $M_O = F\,r = (80)(0.5) = 40\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$.
Problem 5
Ch. 4 · Q5 — 3-D moment of a cable force about a point
A vertical pole stands along the $z$-axis with its base at the origin $O$ and its top at $A(0,\ 0,\ 6)\ \mathrm{m}$. A cable runs from $A$ to a ground anchor at $B(2,\ -3,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$ and carries a tension $T = 700\ \mathrm{N}$, which pulls on the pole at $A$ in the direction from $A$ toward $B$.
Pole OA with cable AB
Determine the magnitude of the moment of the cable force about the base $O$.
Solution
2160 N·m
Free-body diagram
Pole isolated with the cable force as a Cartesian vector at A
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the pole alone with axes at $O$, the position vector $\mathbf{r}_{OA}$ up the pole, and the cable force $\mathbf{F}$ at $A$ pointing toward $B$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $A(0,0,6)\ \mathrm{m}$, $B(2,-3,0)\ \mathrm{m}$, $T = 700\ \mathrm{N}$ from $A$ toward $B$. Find the magnitude $M_O$.
Step 3Isolate the body: The cable force at $A$ is the only load whose moment is asked for; the support reactions at $O$ act at $O$ and do not enter.
Step 4Write the cable position vector: Subtract tail from tip, $$\mathbf{r}_{AB} = \{(2-0)\mathbf{i} + (-3-0)\mathbf{j} + (0-6)\mathbf{k}\} = \{2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 6\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 5Find the cable length: $$r_{AB} = \sqrt{2^2 + (-3)^2 + (-6)^2} = 7\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 6Form the unit vector: $$\mathbf{u}_{AB} = \tfrac{2}{7}\mathbf{i} - \tfrac{3}{7}\mathbf{j} - \tfrac{6}{7}\mathbf{k}$$
Step 7Write the force as a Cartesian vector: $$\mathbf{F} = 700\,\mathbf{u}_{AB} = \{200\mathbf{i} - 300\mathbf{j} - 600\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 8Choose the position vector for the moment: Any vector from $O$ to the line of action works; the simplest is $\mathbf{r}_{OA} = \{6\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 9Write the governing equation: $$\mathbf{M}_O = \mathbf{r}_{OA}\times\mathbf{F} = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0 & 0 & 6\\ 200 & -300 & -600\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 10Expand the $\mathbf{i}$ component: $$M_x = (0)(-600) - (6)(-300) = 1800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11Expand the $\mathbf{j}$ component: $$M_y = -\left[(0)(-600) - (6)(200)\right] = 1200\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12Expand the $\mathbf{k}$ component: $$M_z = (0)(-300) - (0)(200) = 0$$
Step 13Compute the magnitude: $$M_O = \sqrt{1800^2 + 1200^2} = 2163\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 14State the result: $M_O = 2.16(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, with $\mathbf{M}_O = \{1800\mathbf{i} + 1200\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$.
Step 15Check reasonableness: The $-600\,\mathbf{k}$ component acts along the pole and creates no moment about $O$; only the horizontal part, $\sqrt{200^2+300^2} = 360.6\ \mathrm{N}$, acts with a $6\ \mathrm{m}$ arm, giving $(360.6)(6) = 2163\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$.
Worked Solution
Pole isolated with the cable force as a Cartesian vector at A
**Direction of the force:** $\mathbf{r}_{AB} = \{(2-0)\mathbf{i} + (-3-0)\mathbf{j} + (0-6)\mathbf{k}\} = \{2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 6\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $r_{AB} = \sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2} = 7\ \mathrm{m}$. $$\mathbf{F} = 700\left(\tfrac{2}{7}\mathbf{i} - \tfrac{3}{7}\mathbf{j} - \tfrac{6}{7}\mathbf{k}\right) = \{200\mathbf{i} - 300\mathbf{j} - 600\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$ **Moment:** with $\mathbf{r}_{OA} = \{6\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $$\mathbf{M}_O = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0 & 0 & 6\\ 200 & -300 & -600\end{vmatrix} = \left[0 - (6)(-300)\right]\mathbf{i} - \left[0 - (6)(200)\right]\mathbf{j} + 0\,\mathbf{k} = \{1800\mathbf{i} + 1200\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $$M_O = \sqrt{1800^2 + 1200^2} = 2163\ \mathrm{N\cdot m} \approx 2.16(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Problem 6
Ch. 4 · Q6 — Perpendicular distance from a 3-D moment
A force of magnitude $F = 450\ \mathrm{N}$ acts on a pipe assembly at $C(3,\ 4,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$ and is directed from $C$ toward point $D(1,\ 0,\ 4)\ \mathrm{m}$. The assembly is fixed at the origin $O$.
Force along line CD acting on a pipe assembly fixed at O
Determine the perpendicular (shortest) distance $d$ from $O$ to the line of action of $F$.
Solution
3.40 m
Free-body diagram
Position vector, force vector and perpendicular distance d
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch axes at $O$, the position vector $\mathbf{r}_{OC}$, the force $\mathbf{F}$ at $C$ pointing toward $D$, its dashed line of action, and the unknown perpendicular distance $d$ from $O$ to that line.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $C(3,4,0)\ \mathrm{m}$, $D(1,0,4)\ \mathrm{m}$, $F = 450\ \mathrm{N}$ from $C$ toward $D$. Find $d$.
Step 3Plan the solution: The magnitude of a moment is $M_O = F\,d$, so find $\mathbf{M}_O$ with the cross product and then divide its magnitude by $F$.
Step 4Write the direction vector: $$\mathbf{r}_{CD} = \{(1-3)\mathbf{i} + (0-4)\mathbf{j} + (4-0)\mathbf{k}\} = \{-2\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 5Find its length: $$r_{CD} = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-4)^2 + 4^2} = 6\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 6Write the force as a Cartesian vector: $$\mathbf{F} = 450\left(\frac{\mathbf{r}_{CD}}{6}\right) = \{-150\mathbf{i} - 300\mathbf{j} + 300\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7Choose the position vector: From $O$ to a point on the line of action, $\mathbf{r}_{OC} = \{3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 0\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 8Write the governing equation: $$\mathbf{M}_O = \mathbf{r}_{OC}\times\mathbf{F} = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 3 & 4 & 0\\ -150 & -300 & 300\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 9Expand the $\mathbf{i}$ component: $$M_x = (4)(300) - (0)(-300) = 1200\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 10Expand the $\mathbf{j}$ component: $$M_y = -\left[(3)(300) - (0)(-150)\right] = -900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11Expand the $\mathbf{k}$ component: $$M_z = (3)(-300) - (4)(-150) = -300\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12Compute the magnitude: $$M_O = \sqrt{1200^2 + (-900)^2 + (-300)^2} = 1529.7\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 13Relate moment to distance: Because $M_O = F\,d$ with $d$ perpendicular to the line of action, $$d = \frac{M_O}{F}$$
Step 14Substitute and solve: $$d = \frac{1529.7\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}}{450\ \mathrm{N}} = 3.40\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 15Check reasonableness: $d$ can never exceed the distance from $O$ to $C$, which is $\sqrt{3^2+4^2} = 5\ \mathrm{m}$; $3.40\ \mathrm{m} < 5\ \mathrm{m}$, and the units $\mathrm{N\cdot m}/\mathrm{N} = \mathrm{m}$ are correct.
Worked Solution
Position vector, force vector and perpendicular distance d
**Force vector:** $\mathbf{r}_{CD} = \{(1-3)\mathbf{i} + (0-4)\mathbf{j} + (4-0)\mathbf{k}\} = \{-2\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $r_{CD} = \sqrt{4+16+16} = 6\ \mathrm{m}$, so $$\mathbf{F} = 450\left(-\tfrac{2}{6}\mathbf{i} - \tfrac{4}{6}\mathbf{j} + \tfrac{4}{6}\mathbf{k}\right) = \{-150\mathbf{i} - 300\mathbf{j} + 300\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$ **Moment about $O$:** $\mathbf{r}_{OC} = \{3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $$\mathbf{M}_O = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 3 & 4 & 0\\ -150 & -300 & 300\end{vmatrix} = \{1200\mathbf{i} - 900\mathbf{j} - 300\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $$M_O = \sqrt{1200^2 + 900^2 + 300^2} = 1529.7\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ **Distance:** since $M_O = F\,d$, $$d = \frac{M_O}{F} = \frac{1529.7\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}}{450\ \mathrm{N}} = 3.40\ \mathrm{m}$$
Problem 7
Ch. 4 · Q7 — Principle of moments on a wrench
A wrench is used to tighten a bolt at $O$. The handle is horizontal and extends $0.25\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right from $O$ to the grip point $A$. A force $F = 120\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied at $A$, directed down and to the right at $60^{\circ}$ measured from the handle's axis.
Wrench with a force at 60° to the handle
Determine the magnitude of the moment of $F$ about the bolt at $O$.
Solution
26.0 N·m
Free-body diagram
Wrench isolated with the force resolved along and perpendicular to the handle
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the wrench alone with $O$ marked, and replace $F$ at $A$ by one component along the handle and one perpendicular to it.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $F = 120\ \mathrm{N}$, angle $60^{\circ}$ from the handle axis, $OA = 0.25\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the magnitude of $M_O$.
Step 3Isolate the body: The hand force $F$ at $A$ is the only load of interest; the bolt's reaction acts at $O$ and has no moment about $O$.
Step 4Set axes and sign convention: $x$ along the handle from $O$ toward $A$, $y$ upward, counterclockwise positive.
Step 5Resolve the component along the handle: $$F_x = 120\cos60^{\circ} = 60.0\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve the component perpendicular to the handle: $$F_y = -120\sin60^{\circ} = -103.9\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(downward)}$$
Step 7Identify the moment arms: $F_x$ acts along line $OA$ and passes through $O$, so its arm is zero; $F_y$ is perpendicular to the handle, so its arm is $0.25\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 8Write the governing equation: By the principle of moments, $$M_O = x\,F_y - y\,F_x$$
Step 9Substitute numbers: $$M_O = (0.25\ \mathrm{m})(-103.9\ \mathrm{N}) - (0)(60.0\ \mathrm{N})$$
Step 10Compute: $$M_O = -26.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11State the result: The magnitude is $M_O = 26.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, acting clockwise (tightening a standard right-hand bolt).
Step 12Check reasonableness: If the full $120\ \mathrm{N}$ were perpendicular to the handle the moment would be $(120)(0.25) = 30\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; at $60^{\circ}$ only $\sin60^{\circ} = 86.6\%$ of that is effective, giving $26.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$.
Worked Solution
Wrench isolated with the force resolved along and perpendicular to the handle
**Given:** $F = 120\ \mathrm{N}$ at $60^{\circ}$ to the handle, $OA = 0.25\ \mathrm{m}$. **Components:** along the handle $F_x = 120\cos60^{\circ} = 60.0\ \mathrm{N}$ (its line of action passes through $O$, so no moment); perpendicular to the handle $F_y = -120\sin60^{\circ} = -103.9\ \mathrm{N}$. **Principle of moments** (CCW $+$): $$M_O = (0.25\ \mathrm{m})(-103.9\ \mathrm{N}) - (0)(60.0\ \mathrm{N}) = -26.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ Magnitude $M_O = 26.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, clockwise.
Problem 8
Ch. 4 · Q8 — Moment about a coordinate axis
A valve handle turns about the $x$-axis, and $O$ is a point on that axis at the origin. A force of magnitude $F = 250\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied to the handle at $A(0.1,\ 0.4,\ 0.15)\ \mathrm{m}$. The force has coordinate direction angles $\alpha = 120^{\circ}$, $\beta = 45^{\circ}$ and $\gamma = 60^{\circ}$ measured from the positive $x$, $y$ and $z$ axes.
Valve handle with a force defined by coordinate direction angles
Determine the moment of the force about the $x$-axis, $M_x$ (positive by the right-hand rule about $+x$).
Solution
23.5 N·m
Free-body diagram
Handle isolated with r_OA, the force components and the unit vector along the x-axis
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the handle alone with axes at $O$, the unit vector $\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{i}$ along the $x$-axis, the position vector $\mathbf{r}_{OA}$, and the three components of $\mathbf{F}$ at $A$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $F = 250\ \mathrm{N}$; $\alpha = 120^{\circ}$, $\beta = 45^{\circ}$, $\gamma = 60^{\circ}$; $A(0.1,\,0.4,\,0.15)\ \mathrm{m}$. Find $M_x$.
Step 3Check the direction angles: $\cos^2120^{\circ} + \cos^245^{\circ} + \cos^260^{\circ} = 0.25 + 0.50 + 0.25 = 1$, so the angles are consistent.
Step 4Resolve the $x$ component: $$F_x = 250\cos120^{\circ} = -125\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Resolve the $y$ component: $$F_y = 250\cos45^{\circ} = 176.8\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve the $z$ component: $$F_z = 250\cos60^{\circ} = 125\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7Write the axis unit vector: The axis is the $x$-axis, so $\mathbf{u} = 1\,\mathbf{i}$.
Step 8Write the position vector: From a point on the axis ($O$) to a point on the line of action ($A$), $$\mathbf{r}_{OA} = \{0.1\mathbf{i} + 0.4\mathbf{j} + 0.15\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 9Write the governing equation: The moment about an axis is the triple scalar product, $$M_x = \mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{r}_{OA}\times\mathbf{F}) = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\ 0.1 & 0.4 & 0.15\\ -125 & 176.8 & 125\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 10Expand along the first row: Only the first term survives, $$M_x = 1\left[(0.4)(125) - (0.15)(176.8)\right]$$
Step 11Evaluate the products: $$M_x = 50.0\ \mathrm{N\cdot m} - 26.5\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12Compute: $$M_x = 23.5\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 13State the result: $M_x = 23.5\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, positive about $+x$ by the right-hand rule.
Step 14Check reasonableness: $F_x$ is parallel to the axis and the $0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ offset along $x$ slides the force along the axis, so neither appears in the answer; only $F_y$ and $F_z$ with the $y$ and $z$ offsets contribute, exactly as the determinant shows.
Worked Solution
Handle isolated with r_OA, the force components and the unit vector along the x-axis
**Force vector:** $\mathbf{F} = 250\left(\cos120^{\circ}\mathbf{i} + \cos45^{\circ}\mathbf{j} + \cos60^{\circ}\mathbf{k}\right) = \{-125\mathbf{i} + 176.8\mathbf{j} + 125\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$. **Axis and position vector:** $\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{r}_{OA} = \{0.1\mathbf{i} + 0.4\mathbf{j} + 0.15\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$. **Triple scalar product:** $$M_x = \mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{r}_{OA}\times\mathbf{F}) = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\ 0.1 & 0.4 & 0.15\\ -125 & 176.8 & 125\end{vmatrix} = 1\left[(0.4)(125) - (0.15)(176.8)\right] = 50.0 - 26.5 = 23.5\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ Positive, so the moment is counterclockwise when viewed from the $+x$ axis looking toward $O$.
Problem 9
Ch. 4 · Q9 — Moment about an arbitrary axis
A triangular hatch $BCD$ lies in the horizontal $x$–$y$ plane and is hinged along edge $BC$, where $B(0.6,\ 0,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$ and $C(0,\ 0.8,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$. A cable attached to the corner $D(0.6,\ 0.8,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$ runs to a wall hook at $E(0.3,\ 0.4,\ 1.2)\ \mathrm{m}$ and carries a tension $T = 390\ \mathrm{N}$, pulling on the hatch at $D$ in the direction from $D$ toward $E$. The positive direction of the hinge axis is from $B$ toward $C$.
Triangular hatch hinged along BC with cable DE
Determine the moment of the cable force about the hinge axis $BC$, $M_{BC}$ (positive by the right-hand rule about the direction from $B$ to $C$).
Solution
-173 N·m
Free-body diagram
Hatch isolated with the axis unit vector, r_BD and the cable force at D
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the plate alone with the unit vector $\mathbf{u}_{BC}$ along the hinge from $B$ to $C$, the position vector $\mathbf{r}_{BD}$, and the cable force $\mathbf{F}$ at $D$ pointing toward $E$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $B(0.6,0,0)$, $C(0,0.8,0)$, $D(0.6,0.8,0)$, $E(0.3,0.4,1.2)\ \mathrm{m}$; $T = 390\ \mathrm{N}$ from $D$ toward $E$. Find $M_{BC}$.
Step 3Isolate the body: The cable force at $D$ is the load of interest; the hinge reactions act on line $BC$ and produce no moment about that line.
Step 4Write the axis vector: $$\mathbf{r}_{BC} = \{(0-0.6)\mathbf{i} + (0.8-0)\mathbf{j} + 0\mathbf{k}\} = \{-0.6\mathbf{i} + 0.8\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 5Form the axis unit vector: The length is $\sqrt{0.6^2 + 0.8^2} = 1.0\ \mathrm{m}$, so $$\mathbf{u}_{BC} = -0.6\mathbf{i} + 0.8\mathbf{j}$$
Step 6Write the cable direction vector: $$\mathbf{r}_{DE} = \{(0.3-0.6)\mathbf{i} + (0.4-0.8)\mathbf{j} + (1.2-0)\mathbf{k}\} = \{-0.3\mathbf{i} - 0.4\mathbf{j} + 1.2\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 7Find the cable length: $$r_{DE} = \sqrt{0.3^2 + 0.4^2 + 1.2^2} = 1.3\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 8Write the force as a Cartesian vector: $$\mathbf{F} = 390\left(\frac{\mathbf{r}_{DE}}{1.3}\right) = \{-90\mathbf{i} - 120\mathbf{j} + 360\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 9Choose the position vector: It must go from any point on the axis to any point on the line of action; from $B$ to $D$, $$\mathbf{r}_{BD} = \{0\mathbf{i} + 0.8\mathbf{j} + 0\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 10Write the governing equation: $$M_{BC} = \mathbf{u}_{BC}\cdot(\mathbf{r}_{BD}\times\mathbf{F}) = \begin{vmatrix}-0.6 & 0.8 & 0\\ 0 & 0.8 & 0\\ -90 & -120 & 360\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 11Expand the first-row, first-column term: $$-0.6\left[(0.8)(360) - (0)(-120)\right] = -0.6(288) = -172.8$$
Step 12Expand the first-row, second-column term: $$-0.8\left[(0)(360) - (0)(-90)\right] = 0$$
Step 13Sum the terms: The third first-row entry is zero, so $$M_{BC} = -172.8 + 0 + 0 = -172.8\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 14State the result: $M_{BC} = -173\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; the magnitude is $173\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ and it acts opposite to the right-hand sense about $B \to C$.
Step 15Check with a scalar analysis: The axis lies in the plate, so only $F_z = 360\ \mathrm{N}$ turns the hatch. The perpendicular distance from $D$ to line $BC$ is $0.48\ \mathrm{m}$, and $(360)(0.48) = 172.8\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, which agrees.
Worked Solution
Hatch isolated with the axis unit vector, r_BD and the cable force at D
**Axis:** $\mathbf{r}_{BC} = \{-0.6\mathbf{i} + 0.8\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $r_{BC} = 1.0\ \mathrm{m}$, so $\mathbf{u}_{BC} = \{-0.6\mathbf{i} + 0.8\mathbf{j}\}$. **Force:** $\mathbf{r}_{DE} = \{-0.3\mathbf{i} - 0.4\mathbf{j} + 1.2\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $r_{DE} = \sqrt{0.09 + 0.16 + 1.44} = 1.3\ \mathrm{m}$, $$\mathbf{F} = \frac{390}{1.3}\{-0.3\mathbf{i} - 0.4\mathbf{j} + 1.2\mathbf{k}\} = \{-90\mathbf{i} - 120\mathbf{j} + 360\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$ **Position vector:** from $B$ (on the axis) to $D$ (on the line of action), $\mathbf{r}_{BD} = \{0.8\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$. **Triple scalar product:** $$M_{BC} = \begin{vmatrix}-0.6 & 0.8 & 0\\ 0 & 0.8 & 0\\ -90 & -120 & 360\end{vmatrix} = -0.6\left[(0.8)(360) - 0\right] - 0.8\left[(0)(360) - 0\right] + 0 = -172.8\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $M_{BC} = -173\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; the negative sign means the moment acts opposite to the right-hand sense about $B\to C$ (the cable lifts corner $D$).
Problem 10
Ch. 4 · Q10 — Moment of a couple, scalar
A torque of $18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ is needed to turn a valve handwheel. An operator grips the rim with both hands at opposite ends of a diameter and applies two equal, opposite forces $F$ tangent to the rim. The rim diameter is $0.45\ \mathrm{m}$.
Handwheel turned by a two-handed couple
Determine the magnitude of each force $F$ required to produce the couple moment of $18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$.
Solution
40.0 N
Free-body diagram
Handwheel isolated with the two forces of the couple
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the wheel alone with the two tangent forces $F$ at opposite ends of a diameter, pointing in opposite directions, and mark the distance $d$ between their lines of action.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $M = 18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ and rim diameter $0.45\ \mathrm{m}$. Find $F$.
Step 3Recognize the couple: The two forces are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction and parallel, so they form a couple.
Step 4Note the net force: The forces cancel, $\sum F = F - F = 0$, so the couple produces pure turning with no net push on the stem.
Step 5Find the perpendicular distance: The forces are tangent to the rim at opposite ends of a diameter, so the distance between their lines of action is the diameter, $d = 0.45\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 6Write the governing equation: The moment of a couple is $$M = F\,d$$
Step 7Rearrange for the unknown: $$F = \frac{M}{d}$$
Step 8Substitute numbers: $$F = \frac{18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}}{0.45\ \mathrm{m}}$$
Step 9Compute: $$F = 40.0\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 10State the result: Each hand must apply $F = 40.0\ \mathrm{N}$ tangent to the rim.
Step 11Check reasonableness: $(40\ \mathrm{N})(0.45\ \mathrm{m}) = 18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, and $40\ \mathrm{N}$ is about the weight of a $4\ \mathrm{kg}$ mass, an easy effort for one hand. A larger wheel would need less force for the same torque.
Worked Solution
Handwheel isolated with the two forces of the couple
**Given:** required couple moment $M = 18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$; perpendicular distance between the two forces $d = 0.45\ \mathrm{m}$. **Couple:** two equal, opposite, parallel forces give zero net force and a moment $M = F\,d$. $$F = \frac{M}{d} = \frac{18\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}}{0.45\ \mathrm{m}} = 40.0\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 11
Ch. 4 · Q11 — Resultant of two couples, solving for a force
Two couples act on a horizontal beam. The first is formed by two vertical forces of unknown magnitude $F$: one acts upward at $A$ and the other acts downward at $B$, with $B$ located $1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right of $A$. The second couple is formed by two $2.5\ \mathrm{kN}$ forces applied at the top $C$ and bottom $D$ of a short vertical post, where $C$ is directly above $D$ and $CD = 0.6\ \mathrm{m}$. Both $2.5\ \mathrm{kN}$ forces act along lines with slope 3 vertical to 4 horizontal: the force at $C$ points down and to the left, and the force at $D$ points up and to the right. The resultant couple moment on the beam is to be $2.4\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Beam loaded by a vertical couple and an inclined couple
Determine the magnitude of $F$.
Solution
2.40 kN
Free-body diagram
Beam isolated with the couple forces resolved into components
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the beam alone showing the two vertical forces $F$ at $A$ and $B$, and replace each inclined $2.5\ \mathrm{kN}$ force at $C$ and $D$ by horizontal and vertical components.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $AB = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$; $2.5\ \mathrm{kN}$ forces on a 3-4-5 slope with $CD = 0.6\ \mathrm{m}$; required $M_R = 2.4\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise. Find $F$.
Step 3Set the sign convention: Counterclockwise positive, so the required resultant is $M_R = -2.4\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$.
Step 4Resolve the horizontal component of the inclined forces: $$2.5\left(\tfrac{4}{5}\right) = 2.0\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 5Resolve the vertical component of the inclined forces: $$2.5\left(\tfrac{3}{5}\right) = 1.5\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 6Decide which components form a couple: The $1.5\ \mathrm{kN}$ vertical components act along the same vertical line through $C$ and $D$ (zero separation), so they cancel and create no moment. The $2.0\ \mathrm{kN}$ horizontal components are $0.6\ \mathrm{m}$ apart and do form a couple.
Step 7Moment of the inclined couple: The top force pushes left and the bottom force pushes right, which is counterclockwise, $$M_2 = +(2.0\ \mathrm{kN})(0.6\ \mathrm{m}) = +1.2\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$
Step 8Moment of the $F$ couple: Up on the left and down on the right is clockwise, with $d = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$, $$M_1 = -F(1.5\ \mathrm{m})$$
Step 9Write the governing equation: Couple moments are free vectors and add algebraically, $$M_R = M_1 + M_2$$
Step 10Substitute: $$-2.4 = -1.5F + 1.2$$
Step 11Rearrange: $$1.5F = 2.4 + 1.2 = 3.6$$
Step 12Solve: $$F = \frac{3.6\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}}{1.5\ \mathrm{m}} = 2.40\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 13Check reasonableness: The $F$ couple must supply $3.6\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise, enough to cancel the $1.2\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ counterclockwise couple and leave $2.4\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise: $(2.40)(1.5) = 3.6$. The units $\mathrm{kN\cdot m}/\mathrm{m} = \mathrm{kN}$ are correct.
Worked Solution
Beam isolated with the couple forces resolved into components
**Resolve the inclined forces:** horizontal $2.5\left(\tfrac45\right) = 2.0\ \mathrm{kN}$, vertical $2.5\left(\tfrac35\right) = 1.5\ \mathrm{kN}$. The two vertical components lie on the same vertical line through $C$ and $D$, so they cancel without forming a couple. The horizontal components ($2.0\ \mathrm{kN}$ left at $C$, right at $D$, $0.6\ \mathrm{m}$ apart) form a counterclockwise couple: $M_2 = +(2.0)(0.6) = +1.2\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$. **Couple of the $F$ forces:** up at $A$, down at $B$, $1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ apart, clockwise: $M_1 = -F(1.5)$. **Resultant** (CCW $+$): $$-2.4 = -1.5F + 1.2 \;\Rightarrow\; F = \frac{2.4 + 1.2}{1.5} = 2.40\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Problem 12
Ch. 4 · Q12 — Resultant couple moment in 3-D
Two couples act on a pipe assembly. Couple 1 consists of $\mathbf{F}_1 = \{-200\,\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ acting at $B(0.3,\ 0.4,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$ and $-\mathbf{F}_1$ acting at $A(0,\ 0,\ 0)$. Couple 2 consists of a $250\ \mathrm{N}$ force $\mathbf{F}_2$ acting at $D(0.5,\ 0.6,\ 0.2)\ \mathrm{m}$ and $-\mathbf{F}_2$ acting at $C(0,\ 0.6,\ 0.2)\ \mathrm{m}$. $\mathbf{F}_2$ is parallel to the $y$–$z$ plane with a 3-4-5 slope: its $y$ component is $+\tfrac{4}{5}(250)\ \mathrm{N}$ and its $z$ component is $-\tfrac{3}{5}(250)\ \mathrm{N}$.
Pipe assembly carrying two couples
Determine the magnitude of the resultant couple moment acting on the assembly.
Solution
186 N·m
Free-body diagram
Position vectors between the couple forces and the resulting couple moment vectors
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the assembly with the position vector $\mathbf{r}_{AB}$ from the tail force to $\mathbf{F}_1$ at $B$, and $\mathbf{r}_{CD}$ from the tail force to $\mathbf{F}_2$ at $D$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $\mathbf{F}_1 = \{-200\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ at $B$, $-\mathbf{F}_1$ at $A$; $F_2 = 250\ \mathrm{N}$ on a 3-4-5 slope at $D$, $-\mathbf{F}_2$ at $C$. Find $M_R$.
Step 3Write the governing equation for a couple: $\mathbf{M} = \mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F}$, where $\mathbf{r}$ goes from any point on the line of action of $-\mathbf{F}$ to any point on the line of action of $\mathbf{F}$.
Step 4Position vector for couple 1: From $A$ (where $-\mathbf{F}_1$ acts) to $B$, $$\mathbf{r}_{AB} = \{0.3\mathbf{i} + 0.4\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 5Cross product for couple 1: $$\mathbf{M}_1 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0.3 & 0.4 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & -200\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 6Expand couple 1: $$\mathbf{M}_1 = \left[(0.4)(-200)\right]\mathbf{i} - \left[(0.3)(-200)\right]\mathbf{j} + 0\mathbf{k} = \{-80\mathbf{i} + 60\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 7Resolve $\mathbf{F}_2$ in $y$: $$F_{2y} = 250\left(\tfrac{4}{5}\right) = 200\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 8Resolve $\mathbf{F}_2$ in $z$: $$F_{2z} = -250\left(\tfrac{3}{5}\right) = -150\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 9Position vector for couple 2: From $C$ to $D$, $$\mathbf{r}_{CD} = \{(0.5-0)\mathbf{i} + 0\mathbf{j} + 0\mathbf{k}\} = \{0.5\mathbf{i}\}\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 10Cross product for couple 2: $$\mathbf{M}_2 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0.5 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 200 & -150\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 11Expand couple 2: $$\mathbf{M}_2 = 0\mathbf{i} - \left[(0.5)(-150)\right]\mathbf{j} + \left[(0.5)(200)\right]\mathbf{k} = \{75\mathbf{j} + 100\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12Add the couple moments: Couple moments are free vectors, so add components directly, $$\mathbf{M}_R = \{-80\mathbf{i} + (60+75)\mathbf{j} + 100\mathbf{k}\} = \{-80\mathbf{i} + 135\mathbf{j} + 100\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 13Compute the magnitude: $$M_R = \sqrt{(-80)^2 + 135^2 + 100^2} = \sqrt{34\,625} = 186\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 14State the result: $M_R = 186\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$.
Step 15Check reasonableness: Each couple can be checked as $F d$: $M_1 = (200)(0.5) = 100\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ and $M_2 = (250)(0.5) = 125\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, matching $\sqrt{80^2+60^2}$ and $\sqrt{75^2+100^2}$. The resultant, $186\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, lies between their difference (25) and their sum (225), as it must.
Worked Solution
Position vectors between the couple forces and the resulting couple moment vectors
**Couple 1:** $\mathbf{r}_{AB} = \{0.3\mathbf{i} + 0.4\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $\mathbf{F}_1 = \{-200\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$: $$\mathbf{M}_1 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0.3 & 0.4 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & -200\end{vmatrix} = \{-80\mathbf{i} + 60\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ **Couple 2:** $\mathbf{F}_2 = \{250(\tfrac45)\mathbf{j} - 250(\tfrac35)\mathbf{k}\} = \{200\mathbf{j} - 150\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mathbf{r}_{CD} = \{0.5\mathbf{i}\}\ \mathrm{m}$: $$\mathbf{M}_2 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\ 0.5 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 200 & -150\end{vmatrix} = \{75\mathbf{j} + 100\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ **Resultant:** $\mathbf{M}_R = \mathbf{M}_1 + \mathbf{M}_2 = \{-80\mathbf{i} + 135\mathbf{j} + 100\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, $$M_R = \sqrt{80^2 + 135^2 + 100^2} = 186\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Problem 13
Ch. 4 · Q13 — Moving a force off its line of action
A vertical steel column supports a crane-rail bracket. A downward load $P = 60\ \mathrm{kN}$ acts on the bracket at point $B$, which is $0.15\ \mathrm{m}$ horizontally to the right of the column's centreline. For design, the load is to be replaced by an equivalent downward force of $60\ \mathrm{kN}$ acting along the centreline at point $A$ (at the same height as $B$) together with a couple moment.
Column with an eccentric bracket load
Determine the magnitude of the couple moment that must accompany the force when it is moved from $B$ to $A$.
Solution
9.00 kN·m
Free-body diagram
Equivalent force and couple moment at A
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the original load at $B$ on the left and, on the right, the same force moved to $A$ on the centreline with an added couple moment $M$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $P = 60\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward at $B$; horizontal offset from $A$ to $B$ is $0.15\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the couple moment $M$.
Step 3State the principle: A force is a sliding vector, so it can move freely along its own line of action; moving it to a point off that line changes its external effect unless a couple moment is added.
Step 4State the equivalence condition: The new system must have the same resultant force and the same moment about any point; choose point $A$ for the moment comparison.
Step 5Match the forces: The force at $A$ has the same magnitude and direction as the original, $60\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward.
Step 6Find the moment arm: $P$ is vertical and $B$ is $0.15\ \mathrm{m}$ horizontally from $A$, so the perpendicular distance from $A$ to the line of action is $d = 0.15\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 7Write the governing equation: The added couple equals the moment of the original force about the new point, $$M = P\,d$$
Step 8Substitute numbers: $$M = (60\ \mathrm{kN})(0.15\ \mathrm{m})$$
Step 9Compute: $$M = 9.00\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$
Step 10Decide the sense: A downward force to the right of $A$ tends to rotate the column top clockwise, so the couple moment is clockwise.
Step 11State the result: The equivalent system at $A$ is a $60\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward force plus a $9.00\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise couple moment.
Step 12Check reasonableness: The couple moment is a free vector, so it may be shown anywhere on the column; its size grows in direct proportion to the eccentricity, and with zero offset it would vanish, as expected.
Worked Solution
Equivalent force and couple moment at A
**Given:** $P = 60\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward at $B$; perpendicular distance from $A$ to the line of action of $P$ is $d = 0.15\ \mathrm{m}$. Moving a force off its line of action requires adding a couple moment equal to the moment of the original force about the new point: $$M = P\,d = (60\ \mathrm{kN})(0.15\ \mathrm{m}) = 9.00\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$ Since $B$ is to the right of $A$ and $P$ acts downward, the couple moment is clockwise. Equivalent system at $A$: $60\ \mathrm{kN}$ down and $9.00\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Problem 14
Ch. 4 · Q14 — Equivalent couple moment at a point, 2-D
A horizontal beam has its left end at $A$. It carries: a $600\ \mathrm{N}$ downward force at $1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$; a $900\ \mathrm{N}$ force at $4\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$, directed down and to the right at $50^{\circ}$ below the horizontal; a $250\ \mathrm{N}$ upward force at $6\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$; and a counterclockwise couple moment of $800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$. All forces act on the beam's axis. The system is to be replaced by an equivalent resultant force and couple moment at $A$. Take counterclockwise as positive.
Beam with three forces and a couple moment
Determine the resultant couple moment $(M_R)_A$ of the equivalent system at $A$ (counterclockwise positive).
Solution
-1360 N·m
Free-body diagram
Beam isolated with the inclined force resolved into components
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the beam alone with $A$ marked, the three forces at their distances from $A$, the $900\ \mathrm{N}$ force replaced by horizontal and vertical components, and the $800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ couple.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $600\ \mathrm{N}$ down at $1.5\ \mathrm{m}$; $900\ \mathrm{N}$ at $50^{\circ}$ at $4\ \mathrm{m}$; $250\ \mathrm{N}$ up at $6\ \mathrm{m}$; $800\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ counterclockwise. Find $(M_R)_A$.
Step 3Isolate the body: Only the applied loads listed act in this equivalence problem; no support reactions are involved because we are replacing loads, not solving equilibrium.
Step 4Set axes and sign convention: Origin at $A$, $x$ along the beam to the right, $y$ up, counterclockwise positive.
Step 5Resolve the $900\ \mathrm{N}$ force in $x$: $$F_x = 900\cos50^{\circ} = 578.5\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(right)}$$
Step 6Resolve the $900\ \mathrm{N}$ force in $y$: $$F_y = -900\sin50^{\circ} = -689.4\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(down)}$$
Step 7Identify zero-moment components: $F_x$ acts along the beam axis, which passes through $A$, so it has no moment about $A$.
Step 8Write the governing equation: The couple moment of the equivalent system equals the sum of the moments of all forces about $A$ plus all free couple moments, $$(M_R)_A = \sum M_A + \sum M_C$$
Step 9Substitute numbers: $$(M_R)_A = -(600)(1.5) - (689.4)(4) + (250)(6) + 800$$
Step 10Evaluate each term: $$(M_R)_A = -900 - 2757.8 + 1500 + 800\ \ (\mathrm{N\cdot m})$$
Step 11Compute: $$(M_R)_A = -1357.8\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12State the result: $(M_R)_A = 1.36(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Step 13Check reasonableness: The free couple enters with the same value no matter where it is drawn on the beam. The clockwise terms total $3658\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ and the counterclockwise terms $2300\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, so a net clockwise moment of about $1360\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ is consistent.
Worked Solution
Beam isolated with the inclined force resolved into components
**Components of the $900\ \mathrm{N}$ force:** $F_x = 900\cos50^{\circ} = 578.5\ \mathrm{N}$ (along the beam, passes through $A$), $F_y = -900\sin50^{\circ} = -689.4\ \mathrm{N}$. **Sum moments about $A$** (CCW $+$), including the free couple moment: $$(M_R)_A = -(600)(1.5) - (900\sin50^{\circ})(4) + (250)(6) + 800$$ $$(M_R)_A = -900 - 2757.8 + 1500 + 800 = -1357.8\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $(M_R)_A = 1.36(10^3)\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ clockwise.
Problem 15
Ch. 4 · Q15 — Reduction to a single resultant force
A horizontal beam $AB$ is $8\ \mathrm{m}$ long with $A$ at its left end. It carries: a $4\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward force at $1\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$; a $6\ \mathrm{kN}$ force at $4\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$, directed down and to the left at $60^{\circ}$ from the horizontal; a $2\ \mathrm{kN}$ upward force at $6\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$; and a clockwise couple moment of $3\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ applied at $7\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$. All forces act on the beam's axis. The loading is to be replaced by a single equivalent resultant force.
Beam AB with three forces and a couple moment
Determine the distance $d$ from $A$, measured to the right along the beam, at which the line of action of the single resultant force intersects the beam.
Solution
2.19 m
Free-body diagram
Original loading with components, and the single resultant located at d
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the beam with all loads and the $6\ \mathrm{kN}$ force replaced by components; below it sketch the same beam with a single force $F_R$ crossing the axis at an unknown distance $d$ from $A$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $4\ \mathrm{kN}$ down at $1\ \mathrm{m}$; $6\ \mathrm{kN}$ at $60^{\circ}$ at $4\ \mathrm{m}$; $2\ \mathrm{kN}$ up at $6\ \mathrm{m}$; $3\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ clockwise. Find $d$.
Step 3Isolate the body: Only the applied loads are considered; we are replacing the loading, so no support reactions appear.
Step 4Set axes and sign convention: Origin at $A$, $x$ right along the beam, $y$ up, counterclockwise positive.
Step 5Resolve the $6\ \mathrm{kN}$ force in $x$: $$F_x = -6\cos60^{\circ} = -3.00\ \mathrm{kN}\ \text{(left)}$$
Step 6Resolve the $6\ \mathrm{kN}$ force in $y$: $$F_y = -6\sin60^{\circ} = -5.196\ \mathrm{kN}\ \text{(down)}$$
Step 7Sum forces in $x$: $$F_{Rx} = \sum F_x = -3.00\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 8Sum forces in $y$: $$F_{Ry} = \sum F_y = -4 - 5.196 + 2 = -7.196\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 9Write the moment equation about $A$: $A$ is chosen because $d$ is measured from it and every horizontal component passes through it, $$(M_R)_A = \sum M_A + \sum M_C$$
Step 10Substitute into the moment equation: Arms are $1\ \mathrm{m}$, $4\ \mathrm{m}$ and $6\ \mathrm{m}$; the clockwise couple enters as $-3$, $$(M_R)_A = -(4)(1) - (5.196)(4) + (2)(6) - 3$$
Step 11Compute the moment: $$(M_R)_A = -4 - 20.785 + 12 - 3 = -15.785\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$
Step 12Write the equivalence condition: The single force acting at distance $d$ must give the same moment about $A$; its $x$ component passes through $A$, so $$F_{Ry}\,d = (M_R)_A$$
Step 13Rearrange: $$d = \frac{(M_R)_A}{F_{Ry}}$$
Step 14Substitute and solve: $$d = \frac{-15.785\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}}{-7.196\ \mathrm{kN}} = 2.19\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 15State and check the result: The resultant, $F_R = \sqrt{3.00^2 + 7.196^2} = 7.80\ \mathrm{kN}$ acting down and to the left, crosses the beam $2.19\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right of $A$. A positive $d$ is required because a downward force must sit to the right of $A$ to produce a clockwise moment, and $2.19\ \mathrm{m}$ lies within the $8\ \mathrm{m}$ beam.
Worked Solution
Original loading with components, and the single resultant located at d
**Components of the $6\ \mathrm{kN}$ force:** $F_x = -6\cos60^{\circ} = -3.00\ \mathrm{kN}$, $F_y = -6\sin60^{\circ} = -5.196\ \mathrm{kN}$. **Force summation:** $$F_{Rx} = -3.00\ \mathrm{kN},\qquad F_{Ry} = -4 - 5.196 + 2 = -7.196\ \mathrm{kN}$$ **Moment about $A$** (CCW $+$; $F_x$ acts along the beam through $A$): $$(M_R)_A = -(4)(1) - (5.196)(4) + (2)(6) - 3 = -4 - 20.785 + 12 - 3 = -15.785\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$ **Location:** the single force, placed where its line of action crosses the beam, must produce the same moment about $A$. Only $F_{Ry}$ has an arm there: $F_{Ry}\,d = (M_R)_A$, $$d = \frac{(M_R)_A}{F_{Ry}} = \frac{-15.785\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}}{-7.196\ \mathrm{kN}} = 2.19\ \mathrm{m}$$ to the right of $A$.
Problem 16
Ch. 4 · Q16 — Resultant force of an equivalent system
Three forces act at different points on a flat gusset plate in the $x$–$y$ plane: $F_1 = 800\ \mathrm{N}$ directed to the right along $+x$; $F_2 = 500\ \mathrm{N}$ directed up and to the left along a line with slope 3 vertical to 4 horizontal; and $F_3 = 700\ \mathrm{N}$ directed down and to the right at $60^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. The system is to be replaced by an equivalent resultant force and couple moment at a point $O$ on the plate.
Gusset plate with three coplanar forces
Determine the magnitude of the resultant force $F_R$ of the equivalent system.
Solution
810 N
Free-body diagram
Force components and the resultant at O
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the plate alone with each force replaced by its $x$ and $y$ components, and show the unknown resultant $F_R$ at $O$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $F_1 = 800\ \mathrm{N}$ along $+x$; $F_2 = 500\ \mathrm{N}$ on a 3-4-5 slope, up-left; $F_3 = 700\ \mathrm{N}$ at $60^{\circ}$ below horizontal, down-right. Find $F_R$.
Step 3State the principle: The resultant force of an equivalent system is the vector sum of all the forces; the points of application affect only the couple moment, not $F_R$.
Step 4Set axes and sign convention: $x$ to the right and $y$ upward are positive.
Step 5Resolve $F_2$ in $x$: $$F_{2x} = -500\left(\tfrac{4}{5}\right) = -400\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve $F_2$ in $y$: $$F_{2y} = 500\left(\tfrac{3}{5}\right) = 300\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7Resolve $F_3$ in $x$: $$F_{3x} = 700\cos60^{\circ} = 350\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 8Resolve $F_3$ in $y$: $$F_{3y} = -700\sin60^{\circ} = -606.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 9Sum forces in $x$: $$F_{Rx} = \sum F_x = 800 - 400 + 350 = 750\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 10Sum forces in $y$: $$F_{Ry} = \sum F_y = 0 + 300 - 606.2 = -306.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 11Write the magnitude equation: $$F_R = \sqrt{F_{Rx}^2 + F_{Ry}^2}$$
Step 12Substitute and compute: $$F_R = \sqrt{(750)^2 + (-306.2)^2} = 810\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 13State the result with direction: $F_R = 810\ \mathrm{N}$, acting to the right and downward at $\theta = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{306.2}{750}\right) = 22.2^{\circ}$ below the $+x$ axis.
Step 14Check reasonableness: $F_R$ must be at least as large as its biggest component ($750\ \mathrm{N}$) and smaller than the sum of all three magnitudes ($2000\ \mathrm{N}$); $810\ \mathrm{N}$ satisfies both.
Worked Solution
Force components and the resultant at O
**Components:** $F_{1x} = 800\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_{1y} = 0$; $F_{2x} = -500\left(\tfrac45\right) = -400\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_{2y} = 500\left(\tfrac35\right) = 300\ \mathrm{N}$; $F_{3x} = 700\cos60^{\circ} = 350\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_{3y} = -700\sin60^{\circ} = -606.2\ \mathrm{N}$. **Sums:** $$F_{Rx} = 800 - 400 + 350 = 750\ \mathrm{N},\qquad F_{Ry} = 0 + 300 - 606.2 = -306.2\ \mathrm{N}$$ **Magnitude:** $$F_R = \sqrt{750^2 + (-306.2)^2} = 810\ \mathrm{N}$$ directed at $\theta = \tan^{-1}(306.2/750) = 22.2^{\circ}$ below the $+x$ axis. The resultant force does not depend on where the forces act or on the choice of $O$; only the couple moment does.
Problem 17
Ch. 4 · Q17 — Parallel force system on a slab
A horizontal slab lies in the $x$–$y$ plane with one corner at the origin $O$. Four vertical forces act on it: $F_1 = 500\ \mathrm{N}$ downward at $(4,\ 0)\ \mathrm{m}$; $F_2 = 200\ \mathrm{N}$ upward at $(0,\ 3)\ \mathrm{m}$; $F_3 = 700\ \mathrm{N}$ downward at $(5,\ 6)\ \mathrm{m}$; and $F_4 = 400\ \mathrm{N}$ downward at $(1,\ 5)\ \mathrm{m}$. The system is to be replaced by a single equivalent resultant force.
Slab with four parallel vertical forces
Determine the distance from $O$ to the point $P(x,\ y)$ where the line of action of the single resultant force intersects the slab.
Solution
5.81 m
Free-body diagram
Slab isolated with the four forces and the single resultant at P(x, y)
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the slab alone with the four vertical forces at their coordinates and a single unknown force $F_R$ at an unknown point $P(x,\,y)$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $F_1 = 500\ \mathrm{N}$ down at $(4,0)$; $F_2 = 200\ \mathrm{N}$ up at $(0,3)$; $F_3 = 700\ \mathrm{N}$ down at $(5,6)$; $F_4 = 400\ \mathrm{N}$ down at $(1,5)\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the distance $OP$.
Step 3Set the sign convention: $+z$ upward, so downward forces are negative; moments about the $x$ and $y$ axes are positive by the right-hand rule.
Step 4Sum the forces: $$F_R = \sum F_z = -500 + 200 - 700 - 400 = -1400\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Write the moment rule about the $x$-axis: A vertical force $F_z$ at distance $y$ from the $x$-axis gives $M_x = y\,F_z$.
Step 6Sum moments about the $x$-axis: $$(M_R)_x = (0)(-500) + (3)(200) + (6)(-700) + (5)(-400) = -5600\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 7Write the moment rule about the $y$-axis: A vertical force $F_z$ at distance $x$ from the $y$-axis gives $M_y = -x\,F_z$.
Step 8Sum moments about the $y$-axis: $$(M_R)_y = -\left[(4)(-500) + (0)(200) + (5)(-700) + (1)(-400)\right] = 5900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 9Write the equivalence condition for $y$: The single force at $P$ must give the same moment about the $x$-axis, $$y\,F_R = (M_R)_x$$
Step 10Solve for $y$: $$y = \frac{(M_R)_x}{F_R} = \frac{-5600}{-1400} = 4.00\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 11Write the equivalence condition for $x$: The single force must give the same moment about the $y$-axis, $$-x\,F_R = (M_R)_y$$
Step 12Solve for $x$: $$x = -\frac{(M_R)_y}{F_R} = -\frac{5900}{-1400} = 4.214\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 13Compute the distance from $O$: $$OP = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{4.214^2 + 4.00^2} = 5.81\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 14State the result: A single $1400\ \mathrm{N}$ downward force at $P(4.21,\ 4.00)\ \mathrm{m}$, which is $5.81\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$, is equivalent to the four forces.
Step 15Check reasonableness: The largest load ($700\ \mathrm{N}$ at $(5,6)$) pulls the resultant toward that corner, and the upward $200\ \mathrm{N}$ force near $O$ pushes it farther from $O$; a point near $(4.2,\ 4.0)\ \mathrm{m}$ fits.
Worked Solution
Slab isolated with the four forces and the single resultant at P(x, y)
**Resultant force** ($+z$ up): $$F_R = -500 + 200 - 700 - 400 = -1400\ \mathrm{N}\quad (1400\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{downward})$$ **Moments about the axes through $O$** (for a force $F_z$ at $(x,y)$: $M_x = y\,F_z$, $M_y = -x\,F_z$): $$(M_R)_x = (0)(-500) + (3)(200) + (6)(-700) + (5)(-400) = -5600\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $$(M_R)_y = -\left[(4)(-500) + (0)(200) + (5)(-700) + (1)(-400)\right] = 5900\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ **Location:** $F_R$ at $P(x,y)$ must give the same moments: $y\,F_R = (M_R)_x$ and $-x\,F_R = (M_R)_y$, $$y = \frac{-5600}{-1400} = 4.00\ \mathrm{m},\qquad x = -\frac{5900}{-1400} = 4.214\ \mathrm{m}$$ **Distance from $O$:** $$OP = \sqrt{4.214^2 + 4.00^2} = 5.81\ \mathrm{m}$$
Problem 18
Ch. 4 · Q18 — 3-D equivalent force–couple system
A straight pipe lies along the $x$-axis and is fixed at the origin $O$. It is loaded by: $\mathbf{F}_1 = \{-250\,\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ at $x = 0.6\ \mathrm{m}$; $\mathbf{F}_2 = \{180\,\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ at $x = 1.4\ \mathrm{m}$; a force $F_3 = 200\ \mathrm{N}$ at the free end $x = 2.0\ \mathrm{m}$, lying in the $x$–$z$ plane and directed at $45^{\circ}$ below the $+x$ axis (positive $x$ component, negative $z$ component); and a free couple moment $\mathbf{M}_C = \{120\,\mathbf{i}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$. The loading is to be replaced by an equivalent resultant force and couple moment at $O$.
Pipe along the x-axis with three forces and a couple moment
Determine the magnitude of the resultant couple moment $(\mathbf{M}_R)_O$ of the equivalent system at $O$.
Solution
515 N·m
Free-body diagram
Pipe isolated with position vectors from O to each force
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the pipe alone with axes at $O$, position vectors $\mathbf{r}_1$, $\mathbf{r}_2$, $\mathbf{r}_3$ along the pipe to each force, the three forces, and the free couple moment $\mathbf{M}_C$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $\mathbf{F}_1 = \{-250\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ at $0.6\ \mathrm{m}$; $\mathbf{F}_2 = \{180\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ at $1.4\ \mathrm{m}$; $F_3 = 200\ \mathrm{N}$ at $45^{\circ}$ at $2.0\ \mathrm{m}$; $\mathbf{M}_C = \{120\mathbf{i}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$. Find $(M_R)_O$.
Step 3Resolve $\mathbf{F}_3$ in $x$: $$F_{3x} = 200\cos45^{\circ} = 141.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 4Resolve $\mathbf{F}_3$ in $z$: $$F_{3z} = -200\sin45^{\circ} = -141.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Write the position vectors: From $O$ to each point of application, $\mathbf{r}_1 = \{0.6\mathbf{i}\}$, $\mathbf{r}_2 = \{1.4\mathbf{i}\}$, $\mathbf{r}_3 = \{2.0\mathbf{i}\}\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 6Write the governing equation: Moving every force to $O$ adds its moment about $O$, and free couples carry over unchanged, $$(\mathbf{M}_R)_O = \sum\mathbf{M}_C + \sum(\mathbf{r}_i\times\mathbf{F}_i)$$
Step 7Moment of $\mathbf{F}_1$: Using $\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{k} = -\mathbf{j}$, $$\mathbf{r}_1\times\mathbf{F}_1 = (0.6)(-250)(\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{k}) = \{150\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 8Moment of $\mathbf{F}_2$: Using $\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{j} = \mathbf{k}$, $$\mathbf{r}_2\times\mathbf{F}_2 = (1.4)(180)(\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{j}) = \{252\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 9Moment of $\mathbf{F}_3$: The $x$ component is along the pipe ($\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{i} = \mathbf{0}$), leaving $$\mathbf{r}_3\times\mathbf{F}_3 = (2.0)(-141.4)(\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{k}) = \{282.8\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 10Add the components: $$(\mathbf{M}_R)_O = \{120\mathbf{i} + (150 + 282.8)\mathbf{j} + 252\mathbf{k}\} = \{120\mathbf{i} + 432.8\mathbf{j} + 252\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 11Compute the magnitude: $$(M_R)_O = \sqrt{120^2 + 432.8^2 + 252^2} = 515\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$
Step 12State the result: $(M_R)_O = 515\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$, accompanying the resultant force $\mathbf{F}_R = \{141\mathbf{i} + 180\mathbf{j} - 391\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ at $O$.
Step 13Check reasonableness: Both downward forces bend the pipe about the $y$-axis in the same sense, so their $\mathbf{j}$ terms add; the sideways force bends about $z$; and the applied couple twists about the pipe axis and is the only source of the $\mathbf{i}$ term.
Worked Solution
Pipe isolated with position vectors from O to each force
**Force vectors:** $\mathbf{F}_1 = \{-250\mathbf{k}\}$, $\mathbf{F}_2 = \{180\mathbf{j}\}$, $\mathbf{F}_3 = 200\{\cos45^{\circ}\mathbf{i} - \sin45^{\circ}\mathbf{k}\} = \{141.4\mathbf{i} - 141.4\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$. **Position vectors:** $\mathbf{r}_1 = \{0.6\mathbf{i}\}$, $\mathbf{r}_2 = \{1.4\mathbf{i}\}$, $\mathbf{r}_3 = \{2.0\mathbf{i}\}\ \mathrm{m}$. **Moments:** $$\mathbf{r}_1\times\mathbf{F}_1 = (0.6\mathbf{i})\times(-250\mathbf{k}) = \{150\mathbf{j}\},\quad \mathbf{r}_2\times\mathbf{F}_2 = (1.4\mathbf{i})\times(180\mathbf{j}) = \{252\mathbf{k}\},\quad \mathbf{r}_3\times\mathbf{F}_3 = (2.0\mathbf{i})\times(141.4\mathbf{i} - 141.4\mathbf{k}) = \{282.8\mathbf{j}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ using $\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{k} = -\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{j} = \mathbf{k}$, $\mathbf{i}\times\mathbf{i} = \mathbf{0}$. **Resultant:** $$(\mathbf{M}_R)_O = \mathbf{M}_C + \sum \mathbf{r}_i\times\mathbf{F}_i = \{120\mathbf{i} + 432.8\mathbf{j} + 252\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ $$(M_R)_O = \sqrt{120^2 + 432.8^2 + 252^2} = 515\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$$ (The resultant force is $\mathbf{F}_R = \{141\mathbf{i} + 180\mathbf{j} - 391\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$.)
Problem 19
Ch. 4 · Q19 — Location of the resultant of a trapezoidal distributed load
A horizontal beam $AB$ is $6\ \mathrm{m}$ long. It carries a downward distributed load whose intensity increases linearly from $2\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ at $A$ (left end) to $8\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ at $B$ (right end). The load is to be replaced by a single equivalent resultant force.
Beam AB with a trapezoidal distributed load
Determine the distance $\bar{x}$ from $A$ to the line of action of the single equivalent resultant force.
Solution
3.60 m
Free-body diagram
Load split into a rectangle and a triangle with their concentrated forces
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the beam with the trapezoid divided into a rectangle and a triangle, a concentrated force at the centroid of each, and the single resultant $F_R$ at an unknown distance $\bar{x}$ from $A$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: $w_A = 2\ \mathrm{kN/m}$, $w_B = 8\ \mathrm{kN/m}$, $L = 6\ \mathrm{m}$. Find $\bar{x}$.
Step 3Split the loading: Treat it as a uniform load of $2\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ over the whole beam plus a triangular load rising from 0 at $A$ to $8 - 2 = 6\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ at $B$.
Step 4Magnitude of the rectangular part: The resultant equals the area under the load diagram, $$F_1 = (2\ \mathrm{kN/m})(6\ \mathrm{m}) = 12\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 5Location of the rectangular part: It acts through the centroid of the rectangle, at mid-length, $x_1 = 3\ \mathrm{m}$ from $A$.
Step 6Magnitude of the triangular part: $$F_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}(6\ \mathrm{kN/m})(6\ \mathrm{m}) = 18\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 7Location of the triangular part: The centroid of a right triangle is one third of the base from its tall end ($B$), $$x_2 = 6 - \tfrac{1}{3}(6) = 4\ \mathrm{m}\ \text{from } A$$
Step 8Sum the forces: $$F_R = F_1 + F_2 = 12 + 18 = 30\ \mathrm{kN}\ \text{(downward)}$$
Step 9Write the moment equivalence about $A$: The single force must produce the same moment about $A$ as the two parts, $$\bar{x}\,F_R = F_1x_1 + F_2x_2$$
Step 10Substitute numbers: $$\bar{x}\,(30) = (12)(3) + (18)(4) = 108\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$
Step 11Solve: $$\bar{x} = \frac{108\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}}{30\ \mathrm{kN}} = 3.60\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 12State the result: The loading is equivalent to a single $30\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward force acting $3.60\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right of $A$.
Step 13Check reasonableness: The load is heavier toward $B$, so the resultant must lie to the right of mid-span ($3\ \mathrm{m}$) but to the left of the triangle's centroid ($4\ \mathrm{m}$); $3.60\ \mathrm{m}$ falls in between.
Worked Solution
Load split into a rectangle and a triangle with their concentrated forces
**Split the load:** rectangle of intensity $2\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ plus triangle with peak $8 - 2 = 6\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ at $B$. **Rectangle:** $F_1 = (2\ \mathrm{kN/m})(6\ \mathrm{m}) = 12\ \mathrm{kN}$ at $x_1 = 3\ \mathrm{m}$. **Triangle:** $F_2 = \tfrac12(6\ \mathrm{kN/m})(6\ \mathrm{m}) = 18\ \mathrm{kN}$ at one third of the base from the tall end: $x_2 = 6 - \tfrac13(6) = 4\ \mathrm{m}$. **Resultant:** $F_R = 12 + 18 = 30\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward. **Location** (moments about $A$): $$\bar{x}\,F_R = F_1x_1 + F_2x_2 \;\Rightarrow\; \bar{x} = \frac{(12)(3) + (18)(4)}{30} = \frac{108}{30} = 3.60\ \mathrm{m}$$
Problem 20
Ch. 4 · Q20 — Equivalent force–couple system for distributed loading
A horizontal cantilever beam is fixed at its left end $O$ and is $6\ \mathrm{m}$ long. It carries a downward distributed load that increases linearly from zero at $O$ to a peak of $3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ at $4\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$, then decreases linearly to zero at the free end ($6\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$). A concentrated downward force of $5\ \mathrm{kN}$ also acts at the free end. The loading is to be replaced by an equivalent resultant force and couple moment at $O$.
Cantilever with a two-triangle distributed load and an end force
Determine the magnitude of the resultant couple moment $(M_R)_O$ of the equivalent system at $O$.
Solution
60.0 kN·m
Free-body diagram
Distributed load replaced by concentrated forces, with moment arms from O
Step 1Draw the diagram: Sketch the beam alone with $O$ marked, the distributed load replaced by one concentrated force for each triangle, and the $5\ \mathrm{kN}$ end force, each with its distance from $O$.
Step 2List knowns and unknown: Peak intensity $3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ at $4\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$; load is zero at $O$ and at $6\ \mathrm{m}$; $5\ \mathrm{kN}$ down at $6\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the magnitude of $(M_R)_O$.
Step 3Set the sign convention: $x$ to the right from $O$, $y$ up, counterclockwise positive.
Step 4Split the loading: Divide the distributed load at the peak into a left triangle (base $4\ \mathrm{m}$) and a right triangle (base $2\ \mathrm{m}$), both of height $3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$.
Step 5Magnitude of the left triangle: $$F_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}(4\ \mathrm{m})(3\ \mathrm{kN/m}) = 6\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 6Location of the left triangle: Its centroid is one third of the base from the tall side, i.e. two thirds of the base from $O$, $$x_1 = \tfrac{2}{3}(4) = 2.667\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 7Magnitude of the right triangle: $$F_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}(2\ \mathrm{m})(3\ \mathrm{kN/m}) = 3\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 8Location of the right triangle: Its centroid is one third of its base beyond the peak, $$x_2 = 4 + \tfrac{1}{3}(2) = 4.667\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 9Sum the forces: $$F_R = \sum F_y = -6 - 3 - 5 = -14\ \mathrm{kN}\ \text{(14 kN downward)}$$
Step 10Write the moment equation about $O$: $O$ is the point where the equivalent system is required, $$(M_R)_O = \sum M_O = -F_1x_1 - F_2x_2 - (5)(6)$$
Step 11Substitute numbers: $$(M_R)_O = -(6)(2.667) - (3)(4.667) - (5)(6)$$
Step 12Evaluate each term: $$(M_R)_O = -16.0 - 14.0 - 30.0\ \ (\mathrm{kN\cdot m})$$
Step 13Compute: $$(M_R)_O = -60.0\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$
Step 14State the result: The equivalent system at $O$ is a $14\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward force and a couple moment of magnitude $60.0\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$, clockwise.
Step 15Check reasonableness: All loads act downward to the right of $O$, so every term must be clockwise. As a bound, $14\ \mathrm{kN}$ acting at the tip would give $84\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$; since most of the load is inboard of the tip, $60\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$ is sensible.
Worked Solution
Distributed load replaced by concentrated forces, with moment arms from O
**Left triangle** (base $4\ \mathrm{m}$, peak $3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$): $F_1 = \tfrac12(4)(3) = 6\ \mathrm{kN}$, acting two thirds of the base from $O$: $x_1 = \tfrac23(4) = 2.667\ \mathrm{m}$. **Right triangle** (base $2\ \mathrm{m}$): $F_2 = \tfrac12(2)(3) = 3\ \mathrm{kN}$, acting one third of its base beyond the peak: $x_2 = 4 + \tfrac13(2) = 4.667\ \mathrm{m}$. **End force:** $5\ \mathrm{kN}$ at $x_3 = 6\ \mathrm{m}$. **Resultant force:** $F_R = 6 + 3 + 5 = 14\ \mathrm{kN}$ downward. **Moment about $O$** (CCW $+$): $$(M_R)_O = -(6)(2.667) - (3)(4.667) - (5)(6) = -16 - 14 - 30 = -60.0\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$$ Magnitude $60.0\ \mathrm{kN\cdot m}$, clockwise.
